source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-22

procedures.title: Gauge set: install to check system operation (Four-Season)
steps: When taking the gauge lines off the compressor fittings, unscrew the adapters from the fittings rather than the lines from the adapters.

procedures.title: Air conditioning performance test
steps: Close doors and windows; have the car indoors or in shade.
Raise the hood and make sure engine exhaust is ventilated.
Put the transmission in NEUTRAL and run the engine at 2000 rpm.
Set the A/C controls for maximum cooling and high blower speed.
Set the temperature control for full recirculated air with all A/C outlets open.
Let the system stabilize for about 10 minutes.
Place one thermometer in front of the grille and another in the right-hand diffuser outlet.
Compare readings with the performance data table for the car.
notes: The test checks whether the system performs satisfactorily and guides diagnosis; the fixed conditions let readings be compared with the standard tables.
Relative humidity is not in the tables: after the run-in on recirculated air and maximum cooling, humidity over the evaporator settles at about 35% to 40% regardless of outside conditions.
If head pressure runs too high at high ambient temperatures, place an 18" fan in front of the car blowing into the condenser.
Higher ambient temperatures give higher readings. In very humid areas readings may approach but not reach the table figures on a good system.
Low-side pressure directly governs outlet temperature; if it is too low, ice gradually forms on the evaporator fins, blocking airflow and reducing or stopping cooling.
The Comfortron and GM Chevrolet Air Conditioner setup variations in the manual do not apply to Corvette.
